scope: Corollary 2 (Exact division and integer square root) of the manuscript “Integer multiplication below n log n” (preprints/Integer-multiplication-below-n-log-n-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 109 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 834f644c3ce67932), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 5-6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are deterministic machines with fixed finite alphabets and fixed finite numbers of one-dimensional tapes performing the following tasks in O(n(lg n)1−κ) worst-case time, for every n ≥ 1. For x, y ∈ {0, 1}n, put a = val(x) and 5 b = val(y). If b > 0, the division machine takes x#y and returns binn(q)# binn(r), where q = ⌊a/b⌋ and r = a − bq. The square-root machine takes x and returns binn(⌊ √ a⌋). Leading zeroes are allowed, and κ is as in Theorem 1.
